title: How PGSimCity Turns PostgreSQL Complexity into a Virtual City 3D Simulation
gist: Nikolay Samokhvalov released PGSimCity, an Apache-2.0 open-source browser tool that maps PostgreSQL 18 internals onto a 3D city — shared_buffers as a 1024-frame grid, a WAL district, a maintenance yard for autovacuum — and lets engineers trigger real failure modes like clock-sweep eviction races and checkpoint storms. The prototype was built through multi-billion-token LLM prompting then manually calibrated against the REL_18_STABLE source, and it embeds PGlite to run real PostgreSQL compiled to WebAssembly in the browser thread.

insights.claim: PGSimCity is an open-source educational tool released by Nikolay Samokhvalov that converts PostgreSQL cluster mechanics into an interactive 3D spatial simulation running entirely in the browser with no local dependencies.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Zero-install browser tooling lowers the acquisition cost of database expertise, a talent-supply factor for the Postgres ecosystem.

insights.claim: The stated purpose of PGSimCity is to bridge the conceptual gap between high-level SQL queries and low-level kernel execution for backend developers, site reliability engineers, and database architects.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Identifies the abstraction gap between SQL and engine internals as the binding constraint on database operational skill, not lack of documentation.
insights.quote: It bridges the conceptual gap between high-level SQL queries and low-level kernel execution
insights.locator: Running entirely in the browser without local dependencies

insights.claim: PGSimCity's core abstraction maps PostgreSQL 18 internals onto municipal districts: client connections enter from the north into the Postmaster supervisor which forks workers along a backend avenue, WAL is routed to an east district with walwriter and walsender, and a western maintenance yard houses checkpointer, bgwriter and autovacuum.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: A reusable spatial mental model for reasoning about which Postgres subsystem is the bottleneck during an incident.
insights.locator: The core abstraction transforms PostgreSQL 18 internals

insights.claim: In PGSimCity the shared_buffers pool is rendered as a central 1024-frame grid alongside wal_buffers, the ProcArray, lock tables and the Commit Log, with storage beneath the city structured as 8 KB page fields, B-trees, Free Space Maps and Visibility Maps.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: The concrete 1024-frame / 8 KB page grounding is what makes the visualisation a calibration tool rather than an infographic.
insights.locator: The shared_buffers pool sits as a central 1024-frame grid

insights.claim: PGSimCity lets senior database engineers and SREs deliberately trigger operational pathologies to inspect engine failure modes, rather than only tracing the happy path of parse, rewrite, plan and execute stages.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Tooling that teaches failure rather than function is the differentiator to look for across the observability and simulation software category.
insights.locator: While backend developers can trace statement lifecycles

insights.claim: Setting shared_buffers to 16 MB in PGSimCity forces clock-sweep eviction races in which backends must write dirty victim pages before reading new data, demonstrating how undersized buffer pools convert reads into blocking writes.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: A concrete, reproducible mechanism linking a single config value to latency collapse — useful for diagnosing managed-Postgres price/performance tiers.
insights.locator: Setting shared_buffers to 16 MB forces clock-sweep eviction races

insights.claim: Restricting work_mem causes Sort and HashAggregate execution nodes to spill temporary files into base/pgsql_tmp, converting in-memory query work into disk I/O.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Memory-parameter starvation silently shifts cost from RAM to storage IOPS — a hidden driver of cloud database bills.
insights.locator: Simulating restricted work_mem causes Sort and HashAggregate

insights.claim: Long-running transactions depress the xmin horizon, starving autovacuum and inducing table bloat, while heavy write bursts trigger checkpoint storms that flood pg_wal with full-page writes across the max_wal_size / (1 + checkpoint_completion_target) threshold.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Two of the most common Postgres production outages traced to explicit, formula-level thresholds an operator can monitor before failure.
insights.quote: Long-running transactions depress the xmin horizon, starving autovacuum and inducing table bloat
insights.locator: Long-running transactions depress the xmin horizon

insights.claim: The initial PGSimCity prototype was built through multi-billion-token LLM prompting before extensive manual calibration against the PostgreSQL REL_18_STABLE source code, according to its creator.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: A working template for the emerging LLM-generate-then-human-verify build pattern, and evidence that token spend at billion scale is now a normal individual-developer input.
insights.quote: the initial prototype was built through multi-billion-token LLM prompting before extensive manual calibration against PostgreSQL REL_18_STABLE source code
insights.locator: On Hacker News, the project sparked widespread discussion

insights.claim: The project sparked Hacker News discussion specifically around AI-assisted software architecture visualisation and cognitive load, with community feedback driving work to reduce UI pop-up density and inspiring a CHSimCity spin-off for ClickHouse.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Fast forking of the format to other engines suggests visualisation-of-internals becomes a standard artifact for database vendors competing on developer mindshare.
insights.locator: On Hacker News, the project sparked widespread discussion

insights.claim: The project plans nightly mutation testing gates to harden its deterministic verification engine against the upstream PostgreSQL REL_18_STABLE branch, treating drift from real engine behaviour as a continuous regression risk.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Continuous verification against upstream source is the credibility test for any LLM-assisted simulation product.
insights.locator: Looking forward, the project's ROADMAP.md outlines

insights.claim: PGSimCity incorporates PGlite to execute real, in-memory PostgreSQL compiled to WebAssembly directly inside the browser's client thread, rather than only mocking engine behaviour.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Full relational engines running client-side in WASM erodes the assumption that every database workload needs a server — watch it as a slow drag on small-instance cloud database demand.

insights.claim: PGSimCity's presentation layer strictly decouples three.js rendering from core state transitions, computing simulation mutations in isolated TypeScript state machines so frame-rate fluctuations never desynchronize internal state.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Render/state decoupling is the architectural pattern that makes 3D simulation trustworthy enough for technical rather than marketing use.
insights.quote: ensuring frame-rate fluctuations never desynchronize internal state
insights.locator: To maintain architectural fidelity, the presentation layer

insights.claim: The roadmap includes aligning the buffer-frame ring-sizing model with PostgreSQL 18's dynamic io_combine_limit and effective_io_concurrency rules, indicating PostgreSQL 18 changed I/O batching behaviour enough to invalidate older buffer mental models.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Signals a real I/O-path change in PostgreSQL 18 that existing tuning playbooks and managed-service defaults may not yet reflect.

insights.claim: The full PGSimCity codebase, documentation and operational test suites are published on GitHub under the permissive Apache-2.0 License, explicitly inviting forks and contributions.
insights.speaker: Olimpiu Pop
insights.so_what: Apache-2.0 rather than a source-available licence means no commercialisation moat — value accrues to the Postgres ecosystem, not the author.
insights.locator: The full codebase, documentation and operational test suites
